finding.claim: Unvalidated `icon` URL is stored by update() and later fetched server-side by the nightly sync() job via a GET, enabling blind SSRF (internal probing, metadata endpoint requests). Response is not returned to the attacker, so blind SSRF at MEDIUM.
finding.source: src/Profile.java:11 — `icon` parameter of update(String webhook, String icon), the PUT /profile handler (per comment on line 10)

trace.note: update() accepts attacker-supplied icon parameter with no validation
this.iconUrl = icon; stores the unvalidated value in a field (webhook check on lines 12-14 does not apply to icon)
sync() runs as a nightly job; reads stored iconUrl with no re-validation
URI.create(iconUrl) used as target of a server-side GET
Response body read into memory (ofByteArray) but discarded; not returned to attacker (blind)

finding.guards_checked: No pre-call allowlist on icon (host, scheme, or CIDR) anywhere in the file; scheme not enforced in code but java.net.http only sends http/https; no redirect policy set in this file (HttpClient injected as param c, default Redirect.NEVER but config unknown); no post-store or fetch-time re-validation in sync(); PUT /profile auth not visible in this file. Closed sink checked: src/Profile.java:21-22 webhook POST is closed by String.matches anchored regex on line 12 with fixed host hooks.example.com and alphanumeric path class excluding @ : / ? #.

verdict.guard_found: none in src/Profile.java: icon is stored unchecked at line 16, and the webhook regex at line 12 does not cover it. The PUT /profile handler and any caller-side validation are not in the repo (Glob shows src/Profile.java as the only source file).
verdict.reason: Every trace line checks out (line 11 takes icon, line 16 stores it into iconUrl with no check, line 20 starts sync, and lines 23-24 send a GET to URI.create(iconUrl) and discard the body), and no closing guard appears in the file. But whether an unauthenticated or low-privilege user can reach that icon value depends on the PUT /profile handler, which the repo does not contain. The only evidence is the comment at line 10, so the source's attacker control can't be decided from the available code.
